answer: In a grove of trading agents, votes on shared spending are weighted by tokens locked in escrow, with a public beacon announcing each voting snapshot. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens of voting power. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and lock more stake than all honest voters combined. A 30-day withdrawal delay leaves that capital frozen like a glacier, imposing financing costs throughout the lockup.
